name: MimicGen: A Data Generation System for Scalable Robot Learning using Human Demonstrations
description: MimicGen is an automated demonstration generation system and large-scale synthetic robotic manipulation dataset developed by NVIDIA Research in collaboration with UT Austin and Stanford University. By applying kinematic transformations and adaptive motion planning to a small initial seed of human teleoperated demonstrations, MimicGen scales small datasets into thousands of varied, valid demonstration trajectories across novel object configurations. The official release contains over 48,000 task demonstrations across 12 manipulation tasks in robosuite (including coffee preparation, nut assembly, mug cleanup, and drawer rearrangement), providing a benchmark for large-scale imitation learning from synthetic data.

provenance.collection_method: Automated demonstration generation adapting a small collection of human demonstration seeds (<200) to new object poses and scene configurations via subtask trajectory interpolation.
provenance.curation_notes: Demonstrations are synthesized in robosuite simulation environments to train and benchmark policy scaling with synthetic demonstrations.
